args.note: Outage over 24 hours earlier this week

args.summary: Customer insists outage was over 24 hours and wants outage compensation despite system policy denial.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.text: My power was out for more than a day during the storm earlier this week. I heard you give a credit for long outages—can I get that?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'd be happy to check into that outage credit for you. Could you please provide your account number and last name?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.text: Account number 100036, last name Rose.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Could you please also provide your date of birth or the last 4 digits of your SSN to verify your account?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.text: My date of birth is 1974-10-13.I’m still waiting on a response.OK, I’ll wait.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I checked our outage records for your address, but unfortunately, that outage did not meet the requirement of lasting over 24 hours, so we aren't able to provide the $25 outage credit for it. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.text: I’m sure it was over a day—can you double‑check the outage duration and apply the credit if it was indeed longer than 24 hours?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I understand your frustration. I've escalated your case to a specialist who can review the outage details further and follow up with you.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.text: OK, I’ll wait.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience. Have a great day!

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
